comment: Dated source entries deliberately NOT given a card, each with a reason. Suppression is part of the coverage design: most release-notes entries do not deserve a card, and without a way to say so every run re-reports the same minor items until the report is ignored. Matching is on the EXACT heading, so a reworded entry resurfaces instead of staying silently suppressed under a stale rule. 'We decided not to' must stay distinguishable from 'we never looked'.

entries.heading: A/B Testing is now Generally Available
entries.reason: Already covered by AC-13, which is literally about batch evaluations and A/B tests. This is a matcher limitation, not a gap: the 5-char stemmer maps 'testing' to 'testi' and AC-13's 'tests' to 'tests', so they cannot match. Suppressed rather than fixing the shared stemmer, which is load-bearing for the gates that block a build — destabilising it to correct one word in an advisory report is the wrong trade.

entries.heading: Integrations: AG-UI Partnership with CopilotKit
entries.reason: A third-party partnership announcement, not an AWS capability a learner needs to hold. The deck teaches what a service does and where its boundaries are; a named integration partner is news about the ecosystem, and it dates faster than anything else in the corpus.

entries.heading: Integrations: LangChain Deep Agents Partnership
entries.reason: Same as the CopilotKit entry — an ecosystem partnership, not a service capability. If integration breadth ever becomes a teachable point it belongs as one card about the integration surface, not one card per partner.

entries.heading: AgentCore is now ISO and CSA STAR Certified
entries.reason: Genuinely relevant to a regulated buyer, and deliberately not a card: a certification list is a drift-prone fact, so it belongs in a fact-governed slot on a compliance or enterprise-readiness card rather than as a standalone card whose whole content is a status that changes. Revisit when that card exists — this suppression is the pointer to it.

entries.heading: Models: Claude Opus 5 Now Available
entries.reason: Model availability in Kiro changes monthly, so a card naming a model is stale by construction. The teachable idea is that Kiro is model-agnostic and the roster moves — one concept card, not one card per model launch. Suppressed as an instance of a pattern, not as unimportant.

entries.heading: Models: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna now available
entries.reason: Same pattern as the Claude Opus 5 entry: a model roster addition. Notable that a non-Anthropic model arriving is the more interesting signal, and that belongs on the model-agnostic concept card too.

entries.heading: IDE: Faster Sessions, Compaction Fixes, and PowerShell Trust
entries.reason: A release roundup, not an announcement. Kiro's changelog titles bundle three unrelated changes per entry ('X, Y, and Z'), unlike AWS release notes which title one feature each. There is no single subject here for a card to be about.

entries.heading: IDE: Session Restore, Performance Optimizations, and Custom Agent Enhancements
entries.reason: Release roundup, same as above. Performance and restore behaviour are product quality, not concepts a field deck teaches.

entries.heading: Agent Optimization Loop capabilities in Public Preview
entries.reason: Already covered by AC-13, whose lead describes exactly this loop: recommendations analyse production traces and eval outputs, then batch evaluations and A/B tests validate the change before rollout. A matcher limitation, not a gap — AC-13 is titled 'Recommendations, batch evals & A/B tests' and shares no distinctive token with this heading, so no match is possible at any threshold.

entries.heading: Tagging and AWS CloudFormation Support
entries.reason: Already covered by AC-19, whose lead reads 'GA brought the enterprise checklist: VPC connectivity across all services, PrivateLink, CloudFormation, and resource tagging.' Another matcher limitation: the card is titled 'Regions & compliance' and shares no token with this heading.

entries.heading: AgentCore is generally available in AWS GovCloud (US-West)
entries.reason: AC-19 is the home for region and compliance posture and already names FedRAMP in GovCloud. The partition is US-only, so in an ANZ field deck this earns a line on an existing card rather than a card of its own. Worth remembering that the region-count discrepancy the deck already records — 20 columns in the feature matrix against 19 SSM parameters — IS this partition, so it is not unrecorded, merely not card-worthy here.
